headline: Last session: Sensex plunged 570 points at close as Indian markets recorded their longest weekly losing run in 25 years.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: Massive en-masse selling of Indian stocks by foreign investors
Global market pressure from surging US Treasury yields and rate hike fears
Concerns over rising oil prices and significant global fund outflows
Sustained bearish momentum leading to a four-session losing streak and 52-week lows
whatHappening: Sensex crashed 1,000 points intraday, hitting a 52-week low and wiping out up to ₹10 lakh crore
Indian benchmarks recorded their longest weekly losing run in 25 years and worst month since March
INOX Group scions filed for two separate IPOs valued at ₹10,000 crore each
Government capped sugar stock limits for dealers at 1,000 quintals ahead of the festive season
summary: In the last session, Indian markets crashed with the Sensex closing 570 points lower amid heavy foreign investor selling. The downturn marked the longest weekly losing streak in 25 years, with indices hitting fresh 52-week lows. Trading is closed today for Gandhi Jayanti and will reopen on Monday, October 5.
